\section*{Inputs of this build}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{3.2cm}p{12.6cm}@{}}
Ball & \texttt{ {{BALL_ID}} }, mass $m = {{MASS_KG}}$ kg, cross-section $A = {{AREA_M2}}$ m$^2$ \\
Motor & \texttt{ {{MOTOR_ID}} }, $N_{\mathrm{enc}} = {{TICKS}}$ encoder counts per motor output revolution \\
Shooter & \texttt{ {{SHOOTER_TYPE}} }, wheel diameter $D = {{WHEEL_D_MM}}$ mm, gear $g = {{GEAR}}$ wheel turns per motor turn \\
Exit-speed factor & $\eta = {{ETA}}$ \\
Mouth & $h_0 = {{H0_M}}$ m above the floor ({{H0_IN}} in), $f = {{FWD}}$ in ahead of the robot centre \\
\end{tabular}

{{CALIB_SENTENCE}}

\section{Geometry and frame}
Work in the vertical plane through the shooter mouth and the centre of the target CELL mouth. Let $x$ be the horizontal distance from the mouth,
$z$ the height \emph{above the mouth} (so the floor is at $z = -h_0$), and use SI units (m, s, m/s). The table and the robot use the
distance $d$ in inches from the robot centre to the CELL; the mouth is $f$ ahead of the centre, so the horizontal distance the ball must cover is
\begin{equation}
  \rho(d) = 0.0254\,(d - f), \qquad f = {{FWD}}\ \text{in}.
\end{equation}
The ball leaves the mouth at launch angle $\theta$ above the horizontal with exit speed $v_0$:
$(x, z, v_x, v_z)\big|_{t=0} = (0,\ 0,\ v_0\cos\theta,\ v_0\sin\theta)$.

\section{Flight model (ordinary differential equations)}
With $V = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_z^2}$ the state $(x, z, v_x, v_z)$ obeys
\begin{align}
  \dot x &= v_x, & \dot z &= v_z, \\
  \dot v_x &= -k_d V v_x - k_l V v_z, \\
  \dot v_z &= -g - k_d V v_z + k_l V v_x.
\end{align}
The drag term is quadratic and opposes the velocity. The lift term $k_l V(-v_z,\ v_x)$ is perpendicular to the velocity
(its dot product with $(v_x, v_z)$ is zero); for $k_l > 0$ (backspin) it pushes a ball moving in $+x$ upwards. The constants are
\begin{align}
  k_d &= \frac{\rho_a C_D A}{2m} = {{KD}}\ \text{m}^{-1}, \\
  k_{l0} &= \frac{\rho_a A C_{L\alpha}}{2m} = {{KL0}}\ \text{m}^{-1}, \qquad k_l = k_{l0} S_r,
\end{align}
with air density $\rho_a = {{RHO}}$ kg/m$^3$, drag coefficient $C_D = {{CD}}$, lift slope $C_{L\alpha} = {{CL_SLOPE}}$ and $g = {{G}}$ m/s$^2$.
The spin ratio is fixed by the spin rate at launch ($\omega r = S_0 v_0$, no spin decay) and clamped:
\begin{equation}
  S_r = \operatorname{clamp}\!\left(\frac{S_0 v_0}{V},\ -S_{\max},\ S_{\max}\right), \qquad S_r = 0 \text{ if } V \le 10^{-9},
\end{equation}
with $S_0 = {{S0}}$ ($+1$ one wheel under the ball = backspin, $-1$ topspin, $(1-r)/(1+r)$ for a dual-wheel shooter with top-to-bottom speed ratio $r$) and
$S_{\max} = {{CL_SMAX}}$.

\section{Numerical integration (RK4)}
Write $s = (x, z, v_x, v_z)$ and $\dot s = F(s)$ for the right-hand side above. One classical Runge--Kutta step of size $\Delta t = {{DT}}$ s ({{DT_MS}} ms) is
\begin{align}
  k_1 &= F(s_n), & k_2 &= F(s_n + \tfrac{\Delta t}{2} k_1), \\
  k_3 &= F(s_n + \tfrac{\Delta t}{2} k_2), & k_4 &= F(s_n + \Delta t\, k_3), \\
  s_{n+1} &= s_n + \frac{\Delta t}{6}\,(k_1 + 2k_2 + 2k_3 + k_4).
\end{align}
Steps are taken until $x_{n+1} \ge \rho$. The height at the target distance is then interpolated linearly between the two steps,
\begin{equation}
  z(\rho) = z_n + \frac{\rho - x_n}{x_{n+1} - x_n}\,(z_{n+1} - z_n).
\end{equation}
The flight counts as failed ($z = -\infty$) if it lasts longer than $T_{\max} = {{T_MAX}}$ s or the ball falls below the floor ($z < -h_0$).

\section{Aim condition and the per-distance tables}
The solver looks for the exit speed $v$ for which the path passes through the aim point at the CELL:
\begin{equation}
  z\big(\rho(d);\ \theta(d),\ v\big) = z_a(d).
\end{equation}
Both $\theta(d)$ and $z_a(d)$ are read from tables $(d_i, y_i)$ by linear interpolation, constant beyond the first and last row:
\begin{equation}
  y(d) = y_i + \frac{d - d_i}{d_{i+1} - d_i}\,(y_{i+1} - y_i), \qquad d_i \le d < d_{i+1}.
\end{equation}
{{ANGLE_BLOCK}}

The aim height $z_a$ (metres above the mouth) of each row is the height of the path of the same integrator at the row's launch angle and
the centre of the scoring speed window, at $\rho = 0.0254\,(d - f)$. The solver therefore returns exactly the table speed at every table distance;
only the interpolation between rows is approximate. ({{AIM_COUNT}} rows; $z_a = {{AIM_Z_M}}$ m median.)
{{AIM_BLOCK}}

\section{Root finding: scan, then bisection}
Let $F(v) = z(\rho;\ \theta,\ v) - z_a$. Without drag or lift, $z = \rho\tan\theta - g\rho^2 / (2v^2\cos^2\theta)$ is strictly increasing in $v$, but with backspin lift near
the vertical ($\theta$ above roughly $81^\circ$, high $v$) the lift pushes the ball back and $z(\rho)$ rises and then falls again. Plain bisection on $[v_{\min}, v_{\max}]$ could then
land on the falling branch or miss the root. The solver therefore first scans upwards, $v_j = v_{\min} + j\,\Delta v$ with $v_{\min} = {{V_LO}}$ m/s, $\Delta v = {{V_STEP}}$ m/s and
$v_{\max} = {{V_HI}}$ m/s, and stops at the first $v_j$ with $F(v_j) \ge 0$. The root is the \emph{lowest} one, the rising branch that the table used. It then bisects $[v_{j-1}, v_j]$
until the bracket is shorter than ${{V_TOL}}$ m/s and returns its midpoint. The solve fails (no result) if $F(v_{\min}) \ge 0$, if no $v_j$ below $v_{\max}$ reaches the aim height, or if the flight budget of
{{MAX_IT}} integrations is used up. A solve costs the scan flights (at most {{SCAN_MAX}}) plus about {{BISECT_N}} bisection flights, each of 100--400 RK4 steps.

\section{Exit speed to wheel and motor rpm}
The exit speed is a fixed fraction of the wheel surface speed, $v = \eta\,\pi D\, n_{\mathrm{wheel}} / 60$, and the wheel turns $g$ times per motor turn, $n_{\mathrm{wheel}} = g\, n$. Hence
the motor output speed in rpm is
\begin{equation}
  n = \frac{60}{\eta\,\pi D g}\,v = \kappa\, v, \qquad \kappa = \frac{60}{({{ETA}})\,\pi\,({{WHEEL_D_M}}\ \text{m})\,({{GEAR}})} = {{RPM_PER_MPS}}\ \frac{\text{rpm}}{\text{m/s}}.
\end{equation}
$\kappa$ is the one constant to retune at the field (\texttt{RPM\_PER\_MPS} in the Java class). With a per-rpm calibration the table rows use $\eta(n)$; the solver uses the single value
$\kappa$ above (the median over the table).

\section{Encoder ticks}
A motor velocity command in encoder ticks per second is $n / 60$ revolutions per second times $N_{\mathrm{enc}} = {{TICKS}}$ counts per revolution:
\begin{equation}
  \text{ticks/s} = \frac{n}{60}\,N_{\mathrm{enc}} = \frac{\kappa N_{\mathrm{enc}}}{60}\,v = {{TICKS_PER_MPS}}\ v.
\end{equation}
